## 2026-11-11 - 20 FPS on a Spartan missions board: portraits baked into pictures
Asked: "why its 20 FPS in mantineia agoge, missions section?"
Why: the non-Minoan comms portraits (dinosaur-headed people, scripts/portrait.gd) were painted from
scratch - dozens of gradient polygons each - 30 times a second for their animation; a missions board
shows nine (~5 ms apiece). Minoan portraits are a traced picture, so the frame-rate tour (in the Minoan
home system) never saw it.
Done: each person is painted once, off screen (SubViewports), into pictures - the backdrop and body,
the head in four frames (the jaw at three openings and a blink) and the scanlines and frame - kept per
person for the session (64 at most); the portrait draws those, the head bobbing and tilting, the
scanline moving, as before. Headless (no renderer) they stay painted live.
Numbers: Mantineia Agoge's Missions tab 20 -> 473-514 FPS (freezing the portraits alone: 264). New
frame-rate tour scenario "space: sparta station, missions (painted portraits)": 542 FPS, p95 2.3 ms
(baseline added). Full suite 205 pass.
Files: scripts/portrait.gd, tests/fps_tour.gd, tests/fps_baseline.json.

## 2026-11-11 - Combined invasions, distress calls, wrecks and salvage, fuel, Electro, war missions, rings, equipment screens
Asked: invasions combine several fleets; stations under attack send distress calls to nearby allied
fleets; destroyed ships and stations leave salvageable wrecks (greyed out, damaged; a salvage item needed);
ships need fuel, stations sell it, a Star Energizer refuels near a star by draining its power; missions to
protect stations from invasions, attack stations, join fleets, attack fleets; the Patcher always opens on
the infographic; the Library's categories as icons without text; ringed planets' rings explorable - a
pocket of space with ice asteroids in great numbers, pirates and NPC miners (defending miners and killing
pirates earn favour); the four spaces named local / planet / solar / galaxy space (galaxy space only
through the galaxy map); ship and automaton modules shown as slots on a picture of the ship / automaton
by area (nose, thrusters, wings...; legs, arms...), like action RPGs; a new Electro weapon - lightning that
leaps between enemy ships with heavy electric damage and a chance to stun, also fitted by NPC ships and
salvageable from their wrecks. Then all benchmarks and tests satisfied.
Done:
- **Fleets** (fleets.gd): an invasion is an event - 2-3 fleets (4-10 ships each) from systems of the
  empire next to a staging system gather there (waiting), then set out together (all there, or after
  GATHER_TIME 120 s): news for the gathering and the setting out. distress(sys, victim, attacker): a station
  under attack (a siege tick, or real ships shooting it in your system - station.gd) calls the idle defence
  fleets of its owner and of allies at war with the attacker (Galaxy.allied: relation 40+, at peace) within
  4 jumps, at most 2, nearest first, once a minute a system; allies go home when no besiegers are left.
  Replaces the old "defenders help within 3 jumps". Fleets keep their own clock (saved).
- **Fuel**: PlayerData.fuel (saved; -1 = full); Shipyard.fuel_capacity by hull class (CLASS_FUEL 60-170,
  starter 100) + Fuel Tank modules (+30 each); a gate jump burns FUEL_JUMP 10 (main.jump_to refuses
  without it), flying 0.05/s (x2 boosting), the afterburner 2 a burst; an empty tank: 35% speed. Refuel at
  any station (Repair tab: fill up at the station's fuel price / 10 a unit; pump fuel cargo from the hold,
  10 a unit), click fuel in the Ship Computer's hold to pump a unit anywhere. HUD: a FUEL bar (red value
  under 10). Star Energizer (equipment, thrusters, 1,800 cr; a toolbar system): on within 1,800 of the
  star's surface, +6 fuel/s, a twisting beam from the star; off when full or out of reach (no star in local
  space).
- **Electro** (new scripts/chain_lightning.gd ChainLightning; Items.WEAPONS "electro": range 600, every
  1.1 s, 30 damage, chain 3 more within 420 at x0.75 each, stun 25% for 1.5 s): instant, a flickering
  jagged bolt (one node, a few polylines, 0.3 s), electric damage (new Gear damage type "electric";
  Faraday Mesh module resists it), leaps only to the firer's foes. Ship.stun / Enemy.stun (drifting, guns
  silent; bosses and creatures shrug off 70%). NPC warships and raiders carry one by class (fighters 8%,
  interceptors 10%, gunships 22%, frigates 25%; saved) and fire lightning instead of bolts.
- **Wrecks** (new scripts/wreck.gd Wreck, shaders/wreck.gdshader): a destroyed ship (not a creature) or
  station leaves its sprite greyed, darkened, scorched, torn through with smouldering edges, drifting and
  turning; gone after 5 min (a station's 15), 14 at most. With a Salvage Rig (equipment, cargo bay, 900 cr)
  click a wreck: the ship flies up, an amber beam cuts it (4 s, a station's 10) - scrap, electronics,
  machinery, fuel, a piece of gear now and then (a station's: lots, 2 gear); a ship with an Electro gives it
  up 60% of the time (fitted to a free wing slot, or sold for parts at 40%).
- **War missions** (missions.gd _fill_war, 40% of a major power's offers when there's something to
  offer): protect (an invasion heading for one of their systems within 3 jumps: destroy N of the invader's
  warships there), strike (an enemy station within 2 jumps: take N% off its condition - your hits count,
  station.gd on_station_hit), join (one of their fleets within 3 jumps: fly within 1,600 of its ships for
  60+ s), attack_fleet (an enemy fleet: destroy N of its ships wherever it goes - kills count by fleet id).
  A fleet gone ends its missions (counted if you'd done some).
- **Rings** (local space): every ringed planet (spec rings > 0.2: Dikte, the generated ringed giants) has a
  beacon on its ring (SignalBeacon, "local space · the ring of X"); entering it (SignalSite "ring", not a
  signal kind - SignalSites.signal_kinds): 100 ice asteroids (new Asteroid kind "ice", AsteroidGen ore
  "ice", item "Ring Ice") along a curving band (an arc of a 26,000 circle, drawn once), 5 miners of the
  system's empire (or independents), raiders every 55-85 s; each raider you kill while miners work: +1.5
  reputation with their empire. Never finishes. Its rocks aren't saved with the system.
- **Spaces**: local / planet / solar / galaxy space - the guide's new page, the site panel ("LOCAL SPACE ·
  THE RING OF DIKTE"), the galaxy map is galaxy space.
- **Equipment screens** (new scripts/equip_doll.gd EquipDoll): the ship drawn large with its areas' slots
  round it, joined by lines (Shipyard.AREAS: nose - weapon modifiers, sensors; wings - weapons, one per
  hardpoint; hull - armour, shields, repair; thrusters - drive modules, one per utility mount; cargo bay -
  racks, tanks, the salvage rig; area_capacity from the class's hardpoint/internal/utility counts; free_for
  replaces free_slots everywhere - outfitting, fitting, wrecks); drag ship gear onto a free slot of its area.
  The automaton's loadout the same way (Gear.AREA_OF_SLOT: head - core, back and legs - passives, torso -
  armour, right arm - weapon, right hand and left arm - weapon mods), in both computers.
- **Patcher**: an entry always opens on its infographic. **Library**: categories in the tree and the room
  tabs are icons only (names and counts in tooltips).
- Speed: rings' ice rocks are baked once into 8 pictures (Asteroid.bake_ice) - the rock shader for dozens on
  screen cost 5 ms of GPU (186 FPS); mining debris bursts limited to one per rock every 150 ms (a 35% chance
  every frame made hundreds of particle bursts at 300 FPS with five miners: ring 302 -> 713 FPS).
- Also: the signal site's inner Wreck class renamed WreckProp; new weapons / systems go on the toolbar's
  first free slot; encyclopedia entry for ice asteroids.
- Guide: spaces, fuel, Electro, wrecks, rings, repair/refuel, outfitting areas, the automaton's screen,
  combined invasions and distress calls, war missions; editor guide: icon categories.
Numbers: 4 new mission kinds; 3 new equipment (Electro, Star Energizer, Salvage Rig) + 2 modules (Fuel
Tank, Faraday Mesh); 5 ship areas, 7 automaton areas; ring 100 rocks; FPS tour 70/70 at 240+ (ring 713,
new scenario); tests: new tests/test_frontier.gd (10), test_signals / test_play adjusted; full suite 215.

## 2026-11-11 - Collisions with the rings' ice asteroids
Asked: "add colisions with the ice asteroids". Done (signal_site.gd, the ring's local space): every ship
there - you, the miners, the raiders - collides with the ice rocks: pushed out of a rock, bounced (45% of
the speed into it comes back), and a hit faster than 90 hurts (0.12 hull per unit of speed over it,
kinetic; at most every half second a ship) with a spray of ice and, for you, a sound and "Hit the ice!".
The rocks don't move, so they're put in a grid once (400 cells) and each ship checks only its cell and the
next ones. Ring scenario 639-653 FPS. Test: test_frontier test_ring_local_space (pushed out, bounced,
hurt). Files: scripts/signal_site.gd, tests/test_frontier.gd.

## 2026-11-11 - Bouncer Plasma; enemies' plasma webs you to them; the Pulse Cannon
Asked: a new weapon, the Bouncer Plasma - a ball of plasma that bounces between enemies, damaging each,
until it webs them together, unable to move far from one another and slowed; then: fired by an enemy, it
webs the player to the enemy ships and slows him; then: the player's starting weapon is called Pulse Cannon.
Done:
- New scripts/plasma_bouncer.gd (PlasmaBouncer + PlasmaWeb); Items.WEAPONS / EQUIPMENT "bouncer" (Bouncer
  Plasma, 1,500 cr, a wing weapon - Shipyard.HARDPOINT_GEAR, sold at Outfitting; range 620, every 1.8 s,
  16 heat damage a hit, speed 760). The ball homes on its target, hits it and bounces on to the nearest
  enemy within 460 it hasn't hit yet (all hit: the nearest but the one it just left), up to 6 hits; then
  bursts into a web: every ship it hit tied together for 6 s - speed capped at 45%, held within 220 + 30 a

  held to them; "Webbed by plasma - you're tied to their ships!").
- The starting weapon (id "laser", kept for saves) is named Pulse Cannon: the item, the weapon, its
  description, the encyclopedia, the tutorial, the guide.
- Guide: Bouncer Plasma. Icon: three linked plasma balls.
Tests: test_frontier test_bouncer_plasma (bounces over all three, some twice, the web slows and holds) and

## 2026-11-11 - Beam Emitter; the Pulse Cannon's even split
Asked: a new weapon, the beam emitter - a continuous beam that drains shields fast and does less damage
to the hull; the Pulse Cannon does equal damage to hull and shield.
Done: Gear.SHIELD_HULL / Gear.split(dtype, shields, amount): how a damage type splits between shields and
hull - "beam" x2 on shields, x0.35 on the hull once they're down; every other type (the Pulse Cannon...)
the same on both. Applied in Enemy.take_damage, Ship.take_damage and Station.take_damage (no shields: x0.35).
New weapon "beam" (Beam Emitter, 1,300 cr, wings): a continuous blue beam (the mining beam's drawing, in
blue) from the nose while the target is within 540 - 34 damage a second of type "beam", dealt ten times a
second (Ship._update_beam); stunned, it stops. The Pulse Cannon's description says it hits both alike.
New damage type "beam" in Gear.DAMAGE_TYPES. Icon: an emitter and its beam. Guide: shields and hull.
Test: test_frontier test_beam_drains_shields (the split's numbers; fired, a pirate's shields drained fast,
its hull untouched while they last). Files: scripts/gear.gd, enemy.gd, ship.gd, station.gd, items.gd,
shipyard.gd, data/docs/game.md, tests/test_frontier.gd.

## 2026-11-11 - The Projection Array
Asked: new equipment, the projection array - it creates two illusions of the ship that disappear as soon
as they're shot; the ship is shuffled between them to confuse enemies.
Done: new scripts/projection_array.gd (ProjectionArray, Decoy, FlashRing); equipment "projection_array"
(2,000 cr, nose area, a toolbar system - 25 s cooldown). Two illusions fly in formation beside you (170 to
each side): your sprite, paint, heading and an identical engine trail (they mirror your thrust and
afterburner). Enemies can't tell: every ship attacking you takes its pick of the three at random, and so
does one that turns on you while they're up - once per projection (Enemy._decoyed). An illusion is in its
own target group, so bolts, lightning and plasma aimed at it hit it - and it's gone (a flicker). Every 4 s
your ship and a live illusion swap places (flash rings on all three hide it; the camera stays on you), and
the formation re-forms - one each side. They last 15 s. Guide: the Projection Array.
Test: test_frontier test_projection_array (two illusions beside you; attackers re-pick; a new attacker picks
among the three; hit, gone; the shuffle trades places; over after 15 s) - it caught the shuffle picking an
illusion just shot down. Full suite 221 (the planet-walk test flaked once; passes alone).

## 2026-11-11 - Save slots; saving on a planet
Asked: the save has no slots - just one save; and it doesn't save that you're on a planet's surface:
loading puts you back in space.
Done:
- SaveGame (rewritten): 6 slots (user://saves/slot_<n>.json); each save keeps a summary (the system, the
  planet if you were on one, your ship, your credits); latest_slot, slot_info, delete_slot,
  queue_load(slot) (-1: the newest - the game-over screen's Load); the old single save
  (user://savegame.json) moves into slot 1 at start-up.
- Menu (main_menu.gd): Save Game and Load open a slot list - a row per slot (its number, where and when,
  ship and credits, or "Empty slot"), Save here / Save over (an occupied slot asks: click again) or
  Load, and a delete button (click twice); Back or Esc closes it. The title screen shows the latest save.
- On a planet: the surface's save data now carries `landed` ({planet, pos} - it saved only the space game
  before, so loading put you in orbit). Loading it, the space scene restores the game, then goes straight
  back down to that planet (SaveGame.space_state for taking off) and the surface puts the pilot where you
  stood (SaveGame.resume).
- Guide: saving. Tests: new tests/test_saves.gd (slots, summary, newest, delete; the old save into slot 1;
  a planet save says which planet and where, and loads you back there). Checked in the game: saved on
  Amnissos 400 from the ship, loaded from the title screen's list - on Amnissos, at that spot.
Files: scripts/save_game.gd, main_menu.gd, main.gd, planet_surface.gd, data/docs/game.md,
tests/test_saves.gd (new).
Then: "implement auto saves and quicksaves" and "also quick load": SaveGame - a Quicksave slot (quick.json)
and an Autosave slot (auto.json) besides the six (they don't change the slot you saved to last).
F5 quicksaves, F9 quickloads (Keybinds actions "quicksave" / "quickload", Flight group - rebindable), in
space or on a planet, with a QUICKSAVED notice on screen. Autosave every 5 minutes (retried 20 s later if it
can't: paused, landing, jumping) - never while you're under attack (main.in_combat: an enemy within 1,600
going for you) - and on docking, on arriving in a system (2 s after), on landing (1.5 s after); "Autosaved
(docked at ...)" in the log. The Load list shows both first (Q, A). Guide: quicksave, quickload, autosave.
Tests: test_saves test_quicksave_and_autosave (their own slots, in the list, newest, loads; in combat; the
keys bindable). Checked in the game: quicksaved, moved 5,000 away, quickloaded - back at the spot; docking
autosaved.

## 2026-11-12 - Talos reorganised: one navigation rail, one-line headers, compact pages
Asked: "go in talos and reorganise the entire gui to optimise for space and make it much more intuitive to use".
Done:
- **One rail for all of Talos** (new scripts/talos_nav.gd, TalosNav). Down the left of every Talos screen is a column of every tool, each an icon with its name:
  - Dialogue, Chapters, Lore, Citizens, Sprites;
  - Scenarios, Library, SVG, Patcher;
  - Exit, at the foot.
  The current screen is lit, and any tool is one click away. Before, each tool had an unlabelled "Back to Talos" button and you returned to the hub to pick another. Unsaved-change prompts still guard every switch.
- **Shortcuts work anywhere.** The rail's shortcuts (Ctrl+1-5 for the pages, F3/F4/F6/F7 for the tools) now work from every tool, not only from the data editor.
- **One-line headers.** Every screen's header is now one line: its name, a note on what it's for (where status messages also appear), and its own buttons. The data editor used to have three rows: a title with 8 unlabelled icons, a long hint line, and a full-width tab bar. The tab bar and the tool buttons moved into the rail.
- **Data editor pages renamed** to say what they hold: QUEST is now Chapters and INTERACTIONS is now Citizens.
- **Dialogue page:**
  - the stage's fields sit two to a row (a 4-column grid);
  - each dialogue line is as tall as its text (TextEdit.scroll_fit_content_height), with its up/down/delete buttons in a row rather than stacked;
  - a stage's line went from about 130 px tall to 40-70 px, and a whole stage now fits without scrolling;
  - the stage list stays put while the right side scrolls;
  - Preview moved to the header.
- **Lore page:** the text box fills the height.
- **Sprites page:** "Reload sprites" moved to the header, with its own icon.
- **Add buttons** (add line, add citizen line) no longer stretch across the whole width.
- **Library:** the rail sits in its own frame on the left, the top bar and browser start past it, and the browser moved up 20 px.
- **SVG Editor:** the Objects list now shares the right column's height with the properties (it was a fixed 220 px under a mostly empty panel).
- **Patcher and Scenario Editor:** the rail plus the one-line header; their status/hint line merged into the header.
Numbers:
- Data editor chrome above the content: 3 rows (about 150 px) down to 1 row (about 50 px).
- Dialogue stage 0 (4 lines): needed scrolling before; now ends at y≈610 of 1080.
- Rail: 84 px wide, 9 tools plus Exit.
- Tests: 226 pass.
Files:
- new: scripts/talos_nav.gd
- modified: scripts/dev_mode.gd, scripts/scenario_editor.gd, scripts/svg_editor.gd, scripts/patcher.gd, scripts/zoo.gd, tests/test_editor.gd, data/docs/editor.md
- test changes:
  - rail buttons are allowed text plus icon, but must have a full tooltip;
  - the Library's "wheel over the view" point moved past the rail.

## 2026-11-12 - Talos: the rail never moves or resizes; switching tools without the lag
Asked: "in talos some of the left panel tabs lag when selected also i want the left panel tabs to never resize and remain stable".

The rail is now fixed:
- It is 92 x 992 px at (44, 44) on every screen.
- Its buttons are a fixed 92 x 64, with clipped text and a fixed 13 px font.
- UI.scale_fonts now skips nodes with the meta "fixed_font". Before, the data editor scaled the rail's labels with the text-size setting and the other tools didn't, so the rail changed size between screens.
- The Library places its rail at TalosNav.AT, in its own frame. It used to sit at (14, 12) instead of (44, 44).

Where the lag came from, measured in a real window, and what was done:
- **Font fallback.**
  - Why: the game's fonts (Godot's default Open Sans and the bundled Rajdhani and Noto Black) lack symbols the UI uses (▲ ▼ ◀ ▶ ✓ ✕ ● ─ → ⟲ ⟳ ⤒ ⤓, and Δ Λ in Rajdhani). Each time text containing one was laid out, Godot asked the system's fontconfig. A perf profile of the Scenario Editor showed 64% of the time in libfontconfig, plus about 12% in libc doing its string work.
  - Done: two small bundled fallback fonts:
    - assets/fonts/DejaVuSans-Symbols.ttf: a 170 KB subset of the arrow, maths, box-drawing, geometric-shape, symbol, dingbat and Greek blocks;
    - assets/fonts/NotoSansMath-Arrows.ttf: 28 KB, for ⤒ ⤓.
  - NeonTheme.install_fallbacks() gives them to the default font and to every bundled font.
  - The Math subset's line metrics were made compact (ascent 900, descent 230). Godot's line height is the maximum over a font's fallbacks too, and its original tall metrics made every line about 4 px taller (the no-scroll test caught it).
  - Licences: DejaVu-LICENSE.txt and NotoSansMath-LICENSE.txt.
  - Effect: picking a scenario went from 361 to 66 ms. This applies to every screen that shows those symbols, in the game too.
- **Scenario Editor's galaxy.** On the first visit it generated a galaxy, and 920 of its 1,000 ms were the economy's 60 warm-up ticks. It now calls Galaxy.new_game(false, map_only = true): systems, stations and planets only. The Library's planets room does the same. A real game always generates its own.
- **Scenario Editor's drop-downs.** They are now lazy (_lazy_pick): each holds only its current choice until opened. This halves the controls in a scenario (3,234 to 1,648).
- **Icon painting.** Icons were painted in script at about 14 ms each (36 of them took 505 ms on a tool's first visit) and only cached in memory.
  - Icons.paint now keeps each painted icon in user://cache/icons/, keyed by a hash of its drawing (VERSION to invalidate), so it is painted once ever.
  - Each layer is painted only inside its bounds.
- **Patcher.**
  - The scan of unpublished changes walked the whole project, about 100 ms. It now runs on a worker thread, and its entry joins the top of the list when ready (the `scanning` flag; the test waits for it).
  - Patch files (5.3 MB of JSON) are now parsed once and re-read only when a file's modified time changes.
- **Sprites page.** About 700 thumbnails were rebuilt on each visit (25-35 ms). They are now built once and kept (5 ms on a revisit).
- **Background preload.** Talos loads the tools' scenes in the background once it opens (TalosNav._warm, ResourceLoader.load_threaded_request).

Numbers (switching to each tool, measured in a real window):

| Tool | First visit before | First visit now | Repeat visit before | Repeat visit now |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Scenario Editor | 1,466 ms | 150 ms | 450 ms | 128 ms |
| SVG Editor | 295 ms | 53 ms | | |
| Patcher | 229 ms | 118 ms | | |
| Library | 268 ms | 103 ms | | |
| Data editor | 30 ms | 30 ms | | |

Tests: 226 pass. FPS tour: 70 scenarios, 0 under 240, none slower than baseline.

Files:
- scripts/talos_nav.gd, scripts/ui.gd, scripts/zoo.gd, scripts/neon_theme.gd, scripts/icons.gd
- scripts/scenario_editor.gd, scripts/galaxy.gd, scripts/patcher.gd, scripts/dev_mode.gd
- tests/test_editor.gd
- new: assets/fonts/DejaVuSans-Symbols.ttf, NotoSansMath-Arrows.ttf, DejaVu-LICENSE.txt, NotoSansMath-LICENSE.txt

## 2026-11-12 - Talos keeps every tool alive; Versions; the Library icon; 240 FPS checked in Talos
Asked:
- "going through talos tabs is still laggy, also make sure everything satisfies the minimum specs of 240 FPS, once you finish publish the changes"
- "in talos the library tab give it a much more appropriate icon"
- "patcher is renamed to "versions" and is move to the top of the tabs, its default view is always inforgraphics"
- "library is the second tab from the top"

**Talos as one host** (editor.tscn, scripts/editor_screen.gd).
- Each tool (Scenarios, Library, SVG, Versions) is built the first time it's opened, then kept.
- Switching only shows one tool and parks the rest: off to the side (x = 100000) for the screens, hidden for the Library's world. Hidden tools have processing and input off, keyboard focus is released, and their canvas layers (direct children) are hidden.
- Moving a screen back costs about 1 ms; showing a hidden one costs about 25 ms, because it is laid out again.
- Nothing is rebuilt and nothing is lost, so switching no longer asks about unsaved changes. Exit (or Esc on a data page) asks for each tool with unsaved work, in turn (exit(); each tool's guard(then)).
- TalosNav.go / open route through the host. When a tool runs as its own scene (tests), the old behaviour applies.
- Tools are told when they're shown (talos_shown): the Patcher adds the scanned "Unpublished changes" then, not while hidden.
- Turning a tool on or off twice is ignored. Hiding twice used to forget which of its layers were showing.

**Data editor pages are kept too.** Each page is built into its own box and shown again as it is, unless something was edited since (an edit counter on `dirty`; Reload marks every page stale). A revisit costs about 1 ms instead of about 10 ms.

**Scenario Editor.**
- Rule cards are added one per frame, so the screen answers at once (_gen cancels an older rebuild).
- Scenarios.reload_if_changed() reads the file only when it changed (by modified time).

**Live-coding watcher** (scripts/live_link.gd, with --live, as the user plays).
- It re-checked every watched file every 0.5 s in one go: a 9 ms frame twice a second, everywhere in the game.
- It now works SCAN_BUDGET_MS (0.3 ms) a frame through a queue: folders listed, files' times checked. It reloads what changed at the end of a pass.

**Versions** (the Patcher renamed; scripts/patcher.gd).
- Its name in the rail and header is "Versions", at the top of the rail with the Library second.
- It always opens on the newest version's infographic (newest()).
- The scanned unpublished changes join the top of the list without taking the view. This also removed a 129 ms frame when they arrived.
- Docs (editor.md) and CLAUDE.md now say Versions.

**The Library's icon** is a bookshelf ("library" in EditorIcons): spines of different heights and colours, one leaning, on a shelf line. It replaces the paw print left from when the Library was the "zoo".

**240 FPS in Talos.** The tour (tests/fps_tour.gd) gained a talos section: 21 scenarios covering every data page, Scenarios, SVG, Versions with its infographic animating, the asset browser, each of the Library's 11 rooms, and switching tools on the rail every 10 frames. Fixes:
- **Asteroids room: 223 to well over 240 FPS.** Its GPU went from 4.3 ms to about 0.7 ms a frame, measured whole-frame. 34 big ray-marched rocks are now each drawn into a small SubViewport (0.6 of their size) shown as a sprite. Each rock refreshes 20 times a second, a few per frame in turn (zoo.gd RockView). The rocks turn slowly, so it looks the same, and live edits still reach their material. Lowering the shader's detail level had saved almost nothing (4.48 to 4.18 ms).
- **Monsters room: 272 to 605 FPS.** The Void Leviathan redrew its tentacles every frame (1.4 ms); now via UI.redraw_due (60 Hz). This helps battles with it in the game too.
- **Switching tools: p95 6.7 to 3.2 ms** (page and canvas-layer work above).

Full tour: 91 scenarios, 0 under 240 FPS, none slower than baseline. The 21 Talos scenarios were added to tests/fps_baseline.json.

Numbers:
- A tool already built opens in about 1-2 ms.
- First opens: Scenarios 150 ms, then cards one per frame; Library about 50 ms; SVG about 10 ms; Versions about 85 ms.
- Tests: 226 pass.

Files: scripts/editor_screen.gd (rewritten as the host), talos_nav.gd, dev_mode.gd, scenario_editor.gd, scenarios.gd, svg_editor.gd, patcher.gd, zoo.gd, editor_icons.gd, live_link.gd, space_monster.gd; tests/fps_tour.gd, tests/fps_baseline.json, tests/test_scenarios.gd; data/docs/editor.md; CLAUDE.md.
